answer: A payout quorum must span three cut-separated regions of the trust graph, like ships leaving a harbor through different channels. A sybil fleet behind one operator can occupy only one side of each cut, so extra identities add weight but never new channels — the quorum cannot form from a single cluster. On top of that, every vertex faces a sublinear payout cap: doubling identities multiplies earnings by ~sqrt(2), never 2. The attacker's cost — stake and per-epoch work per identity — scales linearly, so the economics spiral against them: more masks, thinner margins, until the fleet loses money.
